topic: What if you could borrow a skill for ten minutes?
title: WHAT IF YOU COULD
BORROW A SKILL?

power.rule: ten minutes, but the owner loses it while you have it
power.look: a glowing skill orb passes from hand to hand while a countdown ring drains

script.beat: 1 cold open: three demos, then the promise
script.text: Imagine you could borrow any skill for ten minutes. Not learn it. Borrow it. You sit at a piano, and your hands already know Chopin. You step into an operating room, and a surgeon's muscle memory takes over. You launch a basketball from half court, and the net doesn't even move. Ten minutes of genius. No practice. No years. No failure. For ten minutes, the impossible is ordinary.

What if you could borrow a skill for ten minutes? One rule: while you use it, the owner loses it. The pianist forgets the piece. The surgeon freezes. The champion can't find the rim. And the clock is already running. Ten minutes is shorter than it sounds.

At first, it feels like a cheat code. Ace the exam. Fix the engine. Land the trick. Play the song your grandmother loves. For ten minutes, you are the person you always wanted to be. The skill doesn't just live in your hands. It lives in your head, in the quiet part of your brain that turns thought into motion. You don't just know the move. You feel it coming.

script.beat: 4 the turn: the cost, with one real number
script.text: But here's the cost. While you borrow the skill, the owner loses it. The pianist forgets the piece. The surgeon freezes at the table. The free-throw champion can't find the rim. And there's a reason. Your cerebellum holds about eighty percent of your brain's neurons. It is the part that makes movement smooth and automatic. Borrow that, and you're not copying a talent. You're taking the machinery behind it. That's real. And the person you borrowed from is standing in the dark, wondering what they lost.

Which means the world notices. A coach. A hospital. A stranger who suddenly can't do the one thing they built their life around. They don't know your name, but they know something is missing. The crowd is watching. The cameras are rolling. And the clock is still running. You can't hide a missing skill.

script.beat: 6 the choice: give it back, or keep it
script.text: Now you have ten minutes left. You can finish the performance. Save the patient. Win the game. Or you can give it back, and go back to being ordinary. The person you borrowed from is waiting. And they are not the only one.
Because if a skill can be borrowed, it can be kept. What happens when the clock hits zero, and you don't let go? The orb goes dark. Then it opens its eyes.

science.claim: The cerebellum holds about 80% of the brain's neurons.
science.working: Azevedo et al. (2009) counted 69.03 billion neurons in the cerebellum and 16.34 billion in the cerebral cortex, out of 86.06 billion total. 69.03 / 86.06 = 0.802, about 80%. The cerebellum is only about 10% of brain mass.
science.source: Azevedo et al., 2009, Journal of Comparative Neurology; Herculano-Houzel, 2010, Frontiers in Neuroanatomy
